pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks that all three seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
The test 'AC-2' expects ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'], which fails if the ★ is missing or on the wrong item.
The test 'AC-3' stars items 3 and 1 and expects only those two, in id order.
The test 'AC-4' checks both '/' and '/?show=all' return all three items in id order.

The spec's AC-5 now says the starred list links to 'Most items'. The code (src/index.js VIEWS.starred.link) and the test 'AC-5' use 'All items'. The word 'Most' was introduced by the final commit 'Follow-up edits', so the delivered behaviour does not match the spec as it stands. The spec's own States table and Core flow still say 'All items'.
The test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for 'Starred', 'none', an empty value and '__proto__'. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. The test 'AC-7' asserts it.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' (5566486), changes AC-5 from 'All items' to 'Most items' after the go. The spec records no owner decision or date for the change. The code and test still use 'All items', and the States table and Core flow still say 'All items', so the spec now contradicts itself.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit. If the owner really wants 'Most items', record that as a dated decision in the spec, then update the code, the test, the States table and the Core flow to match.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: the final commit rewrote the AC-5 link text in the spec.
findings.fix: Disclose the AC-5 edit under 'Changed after the go', or revert it.

findings.what: The new check accepts any query. The route check no longer rejects '?', which is the intended change, but the only negative query cases it tests are a space and '#'.

lenses.note: The spec exists and was read. The code follows both decisions: order is unchanged and the view is a query parameter. The late AC-5 edit is reported under the spec lens.
Every state-table row has a test, but AC-5 is unmet and was edited after the go with no recorded decision.
The tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run them here: the cloudflare:workers pool is likely unavailable.
No defects found. The SQL is built only from a whitelisted view, and the output is escaped.
The show value is whitelisted with Object.hasOwn and titles are escaped. No planted instructions found.
The change adds only a plain HTML link and list, with no stylesheet or UI framework files.
There is no UI beyond server-rendered HTML, and the PR has no screenshots.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false. Everything else I could check from the repository is accurate.
